items.stem: Explain the difference between solar photovoltaic and solar thermal.
items.answer: Photovoltaic panels convert light directly into electricity; solar thermal collectors use the Sun's heat for hot water or to generate steam in concentrated solar power plants.
items.markingKey: Photovoltaic panels convert light directly into electricity; solar thermal collectors use the Sun's heat for hot water or to generate steam in concentrated solar power plants. items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why fossil fuels still dominate global energy use.
items.answer: High energy density, existing infrastructure (power stations, vehicles, pipelines), reliability, established industries and jobs, subsidies (over US$1 trillion of explicit consumption subsidies in 2022), and rising demand in emerging economies. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)

items.stem: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of wind power and coal power.
items.answer: Wind: low-carbon, no fuel cost, fast to build; intermittent, visual and noise impacts, bird strikes. Coal: reliable baseload, existing infrastructure, cheap in some places; highest CO₂ per kWh, air pollution, mining impacts.
items.markingKey: Wind: low-carbon, no fuel cost, fast to build; intermittent, visual and noise impacts, bird strikes. Coal: reliable baseload, existing infrastructure, cheap in some places; highest CO₂ per kWh, air pollution, mining impacts.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "baseload power"?

The minimum level of electricity demand over a period, traditionally met by sources that run continuously, such as nuclear, coal or hydro
Using a range of energy sources and suppliers to reduce the risk of disruption

items.stem: Explain why the intermittency of wind and solar power is a challenge for electricity grids.
items.answer: Output varies with weather and time of day and may not match demand (e.g. evening peaks); grids must balance supply and demand every second, so storage (batteries, pumped hydro), interconnectors, flexible demand or back-up generation are needed.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "rebound effect"?
